approachQuestion.prompt:
Time-limited matching spans. Count contiguous intervals with sum target and length between L and U inclusive. Return a count.

Input: a=[1,-1,1,-1], target=0, L=2,U=3. Output: 3.

Constraints: 1 ≤ L ≤ U ≤ n ≤ 200000; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000; |target| ≤ 200000000000. All sums/counts fit 64 bits.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build P[0..n]. At each ending boundary j from 1 to n, insert P[j-L] into a frequency map if j-L ≥ 0; remove one occurrence of P[j-U-1] if j-U-1 ≥ 0, deleting zero counts. Add frequency[P[j]-target] to the answer.
options.feedback: The active starting boundaries are exactly j-U through j-L intersected with 0..n. Frequencies preserve distinct legal starts while expired boundaries are removed.

options.text: Use all earlier boundaries in the map without expiring any or delaying insertion.
options.feedback: For [0,0,0], L=U=2, target=0, there are only two legal intervals; the unrestricted map counts six.

options.text: Enumerate every start and all endings of legal lengths, adding values and testing the sum.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

feedback.reason: Each boundary performs at most one insertion, expiration, and lookup.
details: The allocated prefix array has n+1 entries, dominating memory even when the active map is small. Each boundary causes at most one insert, removal and lookup: expected O(n) total.

Analyze the full stored-prefix method. Hash operations take expected constant time including amortized resizing, not guaranteed worst-case. Include P and map; exclude input and scalar result. Arithmetic is constant time; no recursion.

Building P[0..n] takes O(n). At each of n ending boundaries there is at most one eligible-prefix insertion, one expiration, and one frequency lookup, all expected-amortized constant cost. Total time is expected O(n), not O(nU), because no full length-U start window is rescanned. Worst-case O(n) for every hash behavior is not part of the stated model.

P itself has n+1 entries and is auxiliary even if the active map is small. The map holds only eligible prefix frequencies and is at most linear-sized, so total auxiliary space is O(n). O(U) alone omits P: U can be small while n grows. Supplied values and the scalar interval count are excluded; P, map entries, and scalar scan state are included.
